Rashi on Eruvin 9a:10:1.hebrew: תוך הפתח - כגון מבוי שיש פצימין רחבים לפתחו מכאן ומכאן, והן הן לחיים שלו, צריך להעמיד לחי אחר מבחוץ אם ירצה להשתמש בין הפצימין:
Rashi on Eruvin 9a:10:1.english: Within the opening - For example, an alleyway with wide pitzimin (side-posts) at its entrance on both sides, and these themselves serve as its jambs. If one wishes to use the space between the pitzimin, one must set up another jamb on the outside.

Rashi on Eruvin 9a:11:1.hebrew: דאית בהו ארבע - ברוחב הפצימין במשך המבוי, דכל ד' רשות באנפי נפשיה היא וכרמלית היא ומדרבנן אסורה:
Rashi on Eruvin 9a:11:1.english: That there are four [cubits] within them - In the width of the pilasters along the length of the alleyway, since every four [cubits] is a domain unto itself, and it is a karmelit, and it is forbidden by rabbinic law:

Rashi on Eruvin 9a:12:1.english: To a karmelit - To a valley, which is attached to and combines with its own kind that lies outside of it.

Rashi on Eruvin 9a:14:1.english: Found - A karmelit between the cheeks that did not have the measure of a karmelit.

Rashi on Eruvin 9a:14:2.english: Its own kind - that crosses in front of it.

Rashi on Eruvin 9a:14:3.english: And it was roused - It was strengthened by its own kind and roused from its sleep. Previously it had been nullified in the presence of something not of its kind. A similar case appears in Bekhorot (22a): impurity that was nullified, then returned and was roused.

Rashi on Eruvin 9a:14:4.hebrew: אבל פתוח לרשות הרבים - שלא זה מינו ולא זה מינו, ולכאן וכאן בטלה:
Rashi on Eruvin 9a:14:4.english: But it is open to the public domain - [Meaning:] That neither this one is of the same species as that one, and so it is nullified in both directions:

Rashi on Eruvin 9a:15:1.english: And you should not think [it is permitted] "between the cheeks" - For R. Yochanan, it is forbidden:

Rashi on Eruvin 9a:15:2.english: But didn't R. Yoḥanan say: "An alley that was paved with lechayim (side-posts)" - [Lechayim are set] along the length of the alley, from its head to its end, two or three cubits apart.

Rashi on Eruvin 9a:15:3.english: Less than four - That there is not four between one lechi (side-post) and another lechi, but there is three between them.

Rashi on Eruvin 9a:15:4.english: We have come to the dispute of Rabban Shimon and the Rabbis - That they disputed above regarding [a gap of] three [handbreadths] up to four, whether we say “lavud” [that a gap of this size is treated as closed, so the two sides count as joined] or not. From that same dispute we learn that there is also a dispute between them regarding the validity of this alleyway. R. Yochanan did not explain his statement, and now Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua is explaining it. For, necessarily, what R. Yochanan said, that the dispute of Rabban Shimon and the Rabbis applies here, can only be found with usage opposite the side-posts (lechayim). For according to Rabban Shimon, they are all one side-post, and one may use the alleyway only up to the inner edge of the inner side-post. But from there outward, it is “between the side-posts” and forbidden. According to the Rabbis, they are not one side-post, and with the outer side-post the alleyway is permitted, and one may use the entire alleyway up to the inner edge of the outer side-post, since opposite the outer side-post alone it is “between the side-posts.” Evidently, according to R. Yochanan, “between the side-posts” is forbidden. For if “between the side-posts” were permitted according to R. Yochanan, what would be the relevance of the dispute of Rabban Shimon and the Rabbis here? Whether they are all one side-post or not, the one using it is positioned opposite all of them.

Rashi on Eruvin 9a:1:1.english: A fence - This implies that it is distant from the walls:

Rashi on Eruvin 9a:1:2.english: Or hanging - That is, its ends do not rest on top of the walls. It hangs in the air, falling short of reaching either of its two sides. Such a case is where one plants a reed of any size in the middle of the entrance of the alley and places the beam on top of it, like this:

Rashi on Eruvin 9a:1:3.english: Rabban Shimon holds that in every case, a gap of less than four [cubits] is considered as if it were attached (lavud).

Rashi on Eruvin 9a:2:1.english: Drawn from the outside - that was extended into the public domain, such as the case discussed above of the two pegs:

Rashi on Eruvin 9a:2:2.english: Hanging from the inside - That it is short on two sides and does not reach the walls, but hangs in the air, and we say it is considered joined (lavud) to extend its ends.

Rashi on Eruvin 9a:3:1.english: Both this one and that one are on the inside - we are speaking of a case where both are on a short beam.

Rashi on Eruvin 9a:3:2.english: A hedge on one side - One end rests on the wall, and its other end does not reach the opposite wall:

Rashi on Eruvin 9a:5:1.hebrew: רב אשי אמר - משום ב' רוחות לא איצטריכא ליה, דכיון דתנא משוכה מרוח אחת, הוא הדין משתי רוחות; אלא חדא קתני משוכה, והיא תלויה, שקצרה היא מהגיע לכתלים, ועוד שתלויה היא למעלה מגובה כותלי המבוי:
Rashi on Eruvin 9a:5:1.english: Rav Ashi said - Regarding two directions, it was not necessary for [the Mishna] to teach it, since it taught "a mishucha from one direction," and so the same law applies to two directions. Rather, it taught only "mishucha" and "it is suspended," because it is short and does not reach the walls, and also because it is suspended above the height of the walls of the alley:

Rashi on Eruvin 9a:5:2.english: And what is the case? It is where he drove two crooked pegs atop the two walls of the alleyway - Their bent ends lean toward each other, so that they serve as supports to extend the beam across both sides when it is laid on them. But the pegs themselves are not fit to serve as the beam, since they lack the width of a handbreadth, the minimum width required of a beam in our mishna:

Rashi on Eruvin 9a:5:3.english: And their curvature is not three [tefachim] - One could say that it is considered attached to the ends of the beam and to the walls, and that the height of the pegs above the walls is not three tefachim. For if it were three tefachim, the beam would be disqualified, since we require that the beam rest on top of the walls. But now, since it is less than three, we say: press down the low part, as if it were resting on the wall.

Rashi on Eruvin 9a:5:4.english: Lavud - A term meaning an appendage, to extend; in Old French it is אפש"ק.

Rashi on Eruvin 9a:6:1.english: Is considered a karmelit - And it is forbidden to carry there.

Rashi on Eruvin 9a:7:1.hebrew: מסתברא מילתיה דר' יוחנן - דאמר פוק תני לברא, אלא מותר הוא אתחת קורה, קאמר ליה, דקסבר חודו החיצון יורד וסותם:
Rashi on Eruvin 9a:7:1.english: It stands to reason, the statement of Rabbi Yochanan - who said, "Go and teach it outside [as a baraita]," but rather it is permitted beneath a beam; he said this to him because he holds that the outer edge [of the beam] descends and closes off.

Rashi on Eruvin 9a:7:2.english: But between the cheeks - In an alleyway where there is no beam [across the top], [R. Yochanan] concedes that it is forbidden.

Rashi on Eruvin 9a:8:1.hebrew: מקום שאין בו ד' על ד' - עומד בין רשות הרבים לרשות היחיד, הואיל וליכא מקום חשוב, לאו רשות באנפי נפשיה הוא, ובטיל להכא ולהכא, והיינו מקום פטור:
Rashi on Eruvin 9a:8:1.english: A place that does not have four by four [tefachim] - It stands between a public domain and a private domain. Since there is no significant area, it is not a domain in its own right; it is nullified with respect to both sides, and this is what is meant by a 'makom patur' (an exempt place).

Rashi on Eruvin 9a:8:2.english: To carry upon it (on one's shoulder) - Loads.

Rashi on Eruvin 9a:8:3.hebrew: ובלבד שלא יחליפו - דלא לימרו דקא מעייל מרשות הרבים לרשות היחיד ואתי למישרי הוצאה בשבת, ובין לחיים נמי, אפילו חשבת ליה מקום בפני עצמו, בטל להכא ולהכא ושרי:
Rashi on Eruvin 9a:8:3.english: Provided that they do not exchange - Lest one say that he is bringing [an object] from the public domain into the private domain, and will come to permit carrying out on Shabbat; and [the same applies] between the cheeks as well: even if you consider it a separate place of its own, it is nullified with regard to both here and there, and it is permitted.

Rashi on Eruvin 9a:9:1.hebrew: בגבוה שלשה - דמינכרא, אבל בין לחיים דלא מינכרא דוכתא, אי שריית לטלטל התם אתי להחליף ולאפוקי לרשות הרבים:
Rashi on Eruvin 9a:9:1.english: At a height of three - Because the place is recognizable there. But between the cheeks, where the place is not recognizable, if one permits carrying there, one will come to switch the objects and carry them out into the public domain:

Tosafot on Eruvin 9a:10:1.hebrew: תוך הפתח צריך לחי אחר להתירו - לאו משום דנחשב כמבוי בפני עצמו, דאין מבוי ניתר בלחי וקורה, אלא אם כן ארכו יתר על רחבו, ובתים וחצירות פתוחין לתוכו:
Tosafot on Eruvin 9a:10:1.english: Within the opening it needs another lechi to permit it - Not because it is considered an alley in its own right, since an alley is not permitted by a lechi and a beam, unless its length exceeds its width and houses and courtyards open into it.

Tosafot on Eruvin 9a:12:1.hebrew: ורבא התם הוא דפתוח לכרמלית - ואם תאמר בפרק קמא דשבת (ד' ו.) גבי אחרים אומרים אסקופה משמשת שתי רשויות, פתח פתוח כלפנים, פתח נעול כלחוץ, ופריך מהא דאמר רב: צריך לחי אחר להתירו. ומשני הכא: באסקופת מבוי עסקינן. ואמאי לא משני התם, דפתוחה לכרמלית, וההוא דאחרים בפתוח לרה"ר? וי"ל: דאי בפתוח לרה"ר, כיון דאין בו ארבע על ארבע, הוי מקום פטור, ואפילו פתח נעול נמי כלפנים. ותדע, דלאביי נמי לוקמא בגובה שלשה, דהוי מקום פטור כדאמרינן לעיל. אלא משום דאם כן אפילו נעול נמי:
Tosafot on Eruvin 9a:12:1.english: And Rava [answers]: there, it is open to a karmelit - And if you say, in the first chapter of Shabbat (ד' ו.), regarding the others who say that an askupa serves two domains (an open opening is treated like the inside, and a locked opening like the outside), and [the Gemara] objects from what Rav said: one needs another doorpost (lehi) to permit it. [The Gemara] answers here: we are dealing with an askupa of an alleyway. And why does it not answer there: [the case is one where the askupa] is open to a karmelit, while the case of the others is [one where it is] open to a public domain? And one can answer: if it is open to a public domain, then since it does not have four by four [amot], it is an exempt place, and even a locked opening is also treated like the inside. And know that according to Abaye too, one may establish [it] at a height of three [tefachim], which is an exempt place, as we said above. Rather [the answer is rejected] because if so, even a locked [opening] would also [be permitted].

Tosafot on Eruvin 9a:5:1.hebrew: שאין בגובהן שלשה - ואם תאמר, והא אמר בסוף פרק הישן (סוכה ד' כב.) דכי יש ברחבו טפח אמר חבוט ורמי אפילו ביתר מג', וקורה דרחבה טפח נימא נמי חבוט ורמי אפילו גבוה מג', ובלאו הכי קשה, אמאי לא שריא אפילו ביתר מג' כיון דקורה תוך עשרים? וי"ל דהכא בעינן קורה על גבי מבוי, וביתר מג' לא הוי היכר. תדע, דהא משוכה מבחוץ אפילו בפחות מג' לא אמרינן לבוד:
Tosafot on Eruvin 9a:5:1.english: That there are not three [tefachim] in their height - And if you say: But surely at the end of the chapter HaYashen (Sukkah 22b) [the Gemara] said that when its width is a tefach, [the principle of] chavut vi-rami applies even if it is more than three [tefachim high]; and for a beam whose width is a tefach, let us also say that chavut vi-rami applies even if it is higher than three [tefachim]. And even apart from this, it is difficult: why is it not permitted even when [the partition] is more than three [tefachim high], since there is a beam within twenty [cubits]? And it can be answered that here we require a beam over the alleyway, and [a partition] more than three [tefachim] high does not serve as a valid distinguishing mark (heikhar). Proof of this: for a mashukhah (a fence of stakes) placed on the outside, even when less than three [tefachim] high, we do not apply the principle of lavud.
